exercises.title: D.19. PRACTICE 2 — Ba cách cho một số liệu
exercises.instruction: Với mỗi số liệu, viết ba câu tiếng Anh khác nhau cùng diễn đạt một ý (viết cả ba câu vào ô của số liệu đó).

stimulus.caption: Ba số liệu
rows: Average weekly spending on food in France: $120

checklist: 3 câu dùng 3 cách gọi chủ thể / 3 cấu trúc khác nhau
rubric.sampleAnswer:
1. The percentage of Internet users in Vietnam was 70%, compared to 55% in Thailand.
70% of Vietnamese people used the Internet, while the figure for Thailand was 55%.
Internet usage in Vietnam stood at 70%, 15 percentage points higher than that in Thailand.

2. The unemployment rate in the UK was 8%, twice as high as that in Mexico, at 4%.
8% of British people were jobless, compared with only 4% in Mexico.
The level of joblessness in the UK was double the figure for Mexico.

3. Average weekly spending on food in France was $120.
On average, French people spent $120 on food per week.
Weekly expenditure on food per person in France stood at $120.

exercises.title: PHẦN B — Đề 1 (chọn một trong hai đề)
exercises.instruction: The table below shows the unemployment rate among people aged 16–24 and the poverty rate in four countries in 2010 and 2020 (hypothetical data). Write at least 150 words in 20 minutes. Mục tiêu: gọi tên chủ thể bằng ít nhất 4 cách khác nhau trong bài.

stimulus.caption: Unemployment (16–24) and poverty rate in four countries, 2010 and 2020 (hypothetical data)
stimulus.note: Chỉ cần làm MỘT trong hai đề của Phần B.

checklist: Gọi tên chủ thể bằng ít nhất 4 cách khác nhau
Có so sánh giữa các nước và giữa hai năm
rubric.sampleAnswer:
The table compares four countries in terms of the proportion of 16- to 24-year-olds who were out of work and the percentage of people living in poverty in 2010 and 2020.

Overall, while youth unemployment was by far the highest in Spain, Mexico had the largest share of people living below the poverty line. It is also clear that both rates fell in most of the four countries over the decade.

Spain had the highest level of joblessness among young people, at 41% in 2010, before a slight fall to 38% ten years later. The figure for England was much lower, at 18%, and it dropped to 12% in 2020. By contrast, youth unemployment in Mexico and Vietnam stood at under 10% in both years, although the Vietnamese rate rose slightly from 6% to 7%.

Turning to poverty, 46% of Mexicans were poor in 2010, which was more than twice as high as the figure for Spain, at 21%. Both countries saw only small decreases, to 41% and 20%, respectively. The poverty rate in England fell slightly from 15% to 13%, whereas Vietnam saw the most dramatic improvement, with the proportion of poor people dropping from 14% to just 5%.
commonErrors: lặp “the unemployment rate” ở mọi câu

exercises.title: PHẦN B — Đề 2 (chọn một trong hai đề)
exercises.instruction: The table below shows average yearly spending per person on three items in four countries in 2015 (hypothetical data, US dollars). Write at least 150 words in 20 minutes. Mục tiêu: gọi tên chủ thể bằng ít nhất 4 cách khác nhau trong bài.

stimulus.caption: Average yearly spending per person on three items, 2015 (hypothetical data, US dollars)
stimulus.note: Chỉ cần làm MỘT trong hai đề của Phần B.

checklist: Gọi tên chủ thể bằng ít nhất 4 cách khác nhau
So sánh theo hàng và theo cột
rubric.sampleAnswer:
The table compares how much money people in Sweden, Japan, Canada and Italy spent on average each year on mobile phones, books and public transport in 2015.

Overall, Japanese people spent the most on books and public transport, while Swedes spent the most on mobile phones. Italians had the lowest spending in all three categories.

Sweden had the highest annual expenditure on mobile phones, at $750 per person, followed by Canada and Japan, at $610 and $520, respectively. Italians spent only $430. Spending on books was much lower in most countries, at $260 in Canada, $210 in Sweden and $180 in Italy. Japan, however, was an exception, with $500 per person spent on books.

Public transport accounted for the largest expenditure in Japan, at $980, which was more than twice the figure for Canada ($410). Swedes spent $640 on public transport, while Italians spent the least, at $360.
commonErrors: dùng từ xu hướng cho bảng một năm
